changelog: Add a narrowly scoped Core Principle that downgrades cuts splitting a sentence-initial multiword proper name or an initial NP (2+ content words) to the 'bad' band (15–39), so the scorer prefers leaving the full name/NP intact while not removing early cut options elsewhere.
findings: For cuts that fall inside the same clause the prompt often prefers earlier intra-clause positions, but the better choice is the later cut that completes the clause's predicate so the preceding segment reads as a standalone assertion.
The prompt allows cuts that split sentence-initial multiword names or the head of the initial NP, producing incoherent or misleading preceding stretches.

edits.now: Do not cut inside an initial multiword named entity or inside the head of a sent

diagnosis.why: The inserted rule forbidding cuts inside an initial multiword named entity/NP made the scorer prefer leaving the full initial name/NP intact, which moved many early cuts later. That change improved the top-ranked positions (rank_depth gains at depths 1–3 and positive changes for longer bins ≤10/≤99) but removed useful early cut choices for short-latency bins (small negative by_bin at ≤5 and ≤7), producing roughly balanced wins and losses and a negligible overall mean change.
diagnosis.lesson: A later revision should preserve the benefit of keeping initial multiword names for the top one-to-three cut choices while not eliminating the early cut options relied on by short-latency bins (≤5–7).
